study.question: Does the incumbent buy-context transfer benefit from the signed residual component orthogonal to the product-route cotangent, beyond context-field norm allocation and parallel orientation?
study.hypothesis: The residual route supplies useful angular complementarity to the product route at the shared context embedding output. At fixed per-field cotangent norms, preserving rather than reversing its perpendicular component should improve click AUC under both parallel signs. Parallel reversal is an independent sign control; the four cells identify a conditional angular contrast and interaction. The opposite outcome would motivate a reflected-gradient candidate; neither direction is established by current single-seed summaries.

nearest_work.difference: Immediate local predecessor exchanged total/product field directions and norm allocation. This study fixes native field norms and independently crosses the signs of parallel/perpendicular components of the total cotangent relative to product. It adds no forward architecture or learned capacity.

Archived primary text lines52-93 supports target-conditioned activation pooling; baseline_reference.py implements the local adaptation. Inherit this pooling and its later local extensions. The new intervention is training-only field cotangent geometry, not an original DIN mechanism or exact DIN reproduction.

study.proposed_difference: For each example and equal-width context field, N=R+P, u=P/||P||, A=<N,u>u, T=N-A. Cross +A+T(native), +A-T(orthogonal_reflection), -A+T(parallel_reflection), -A-T(both_reversed). Each field keeps ||N||; a scaled FP32 projection and norm correction implement the reflections without raw squared norms. Native returns N exactly and both_reversed returns -N exactly. If P=0, use N as axis with an exact native fallback for orthogonal_reflection. N=0 stays zero. All four cells execute the same geometry; only the returned buy-to-context VJP changes. Explicit first-order surrogate with unchanged forward and private branch derivatives; no higher-order or novelty claim.
predictions: Under useful signed orthogonal complementarity, native_orientation_bridge exceeds orthogonal_reflection, and parallel_reflection exceeds both_reversed in full-validation click AUC. The average of these two differences is the predeclared orthogonal-sign main contrast.

If the native parallel orientation is useful, native_orientation_bridge exceeds parallel_reflection and orthogonal_reflection exceeds both_reversed. These contrasts and their interaction must be reported rather than selecting a convenient pair.
If reversing the orthogonal component improves over native while reversing both components does not, the reflected-gradient candidate is a useful next hypothesis, subject to paired confirmation.
The native bridge should reproduce g0-r0074-sum_sum_bridge at common state and under the frozen same-seed run; new models have the same expected parameter counts and identical inference operations.
All four task metrics must be reported. Prior click-selected incumbent auxiliary AUCs trail the initial reference; no claim of uniform multitask improvement is predicted.
falsifiers: An absent or reversed orthogonal-sign contrast, with executed geometry confirmed and nondegenerate fields, fails to support useful signed orthogonal complementarity for this implementation.
A benefit only under one parallel sign is interaction-dependent, not a general orthogonal mechanism; report both conditional contrasts.

If native wins against all new variants, retain the incumbent: there is no new performance improvement from this proposal. Conversely, if reflection wins, reject the predicted useful native orthogonal sign and investigate possible harmful transfer.
If new source fails native common-state/one-step parity, field-norm and angle checks, masking, source ownership or resource limits, interpretation is blocked and failed costs remain charged.
If almost all product cotangents are zero or collinear, the orthogonal contrast is weak/unidentified; a null outcome cannot refute complementarity generally.
A single-seed AUC difference, including the historical 0.000004943 buy-summary advantage over native, does not establish repeated support or significance.
alternative_explanations: Single fixed training seed; many validation-adaptive rounds and no independent confirmation. Same-seed parity is not a repetition.
Per-example field norm does not fix combined-task gradients, repeated-ID sparse sums, Adagrad accumulators, global dense clipping or subsequent trajectories.
BF16 casting and FP32 projection/normalization roundoff can perturb exact geometry; host tolerances must pass before interpretation.
Zero product fields use the native direction as reference, so their orthogonal factor is inactive; collinear fields also provide no orthogonal contrast.
Signs are relative to a trajectory-dependent product cotangent, not a direct measurement of alignment with the click gradient.
Host diagnostics may be unavailable; without them no mediated optimizer or field-occupancy claim can be made.
A signed perturbation may change regularization or sparse optimizer cancellation rather than recover semantic representation complementarity.
The latest r0074 interaction can reflect scale/direction trajectory coupling and validation selection rather than independent useful factors.
The incumbent was selected on click AUC, while the auxiliary labels describe category/brand behavior over24h; improvements can trade off auxiliary performance.

FP32 and BF16: at a common initialized state and a common trained/nonzero-output state, compare all four outputs and buffers against parent, on all24 label-order permutations. Four finite[B,1] probabilities; route only label buy. At zero output initialization the intervention can be inactive, so a nonzero-output state is required. Eval must bypass _BuyContextVJP and preserve inference exactly at a common state.

Verify custom forward two exact context clones; private residual/product and all unaffected parameter cotangents equal parent at a common state. Only upstream buy-context output is transformed. Native backward returns (R.float()+P.float()).to(context.dtype) exactly; reverse returns its negative. Native one-step including sparse gradients, Adagrad state and global dense clipping must match parent within declared precision tolerance. Same-seed rerun is parity, not a repetition.

Direct arbitrary-cotangent tests at the split point: shape[B,F*D], D=embedding_dim, widths1/16, B=1 and normal batches. Use zeros, None cotangents, singleton/noncontiguous layouts, P=0, N=0 with R=-P, parallel/antiparallel and orthogonal R/P, mixed-sign, tiny and large finite cases with representable FP32 sums/norms. All results finite. Verify +A-T and -A+T formulas and sign symmetries, per-field norms equal native before cast (rtol2e-5,atol1e-12 for ordinary FP32 scales; report scale-relative error for extremes) and BF16 rounding bound (rtol2e-2 plus scale-aware atol). On nondegenerate ordinary FP32 fields verify normalized parallel projection is retained/reversed and perpendicular component reversed/retained, respectively. Report zero-product, zero-native, collinear and fallback rates if diagnostics interface permits; otherwise mark unavailable. Do not add persistent model counters or hidden input access.
